clue.text: Newsman's focus on that girl's dad, skilled mountaineer

indicators.note: focus means the central point, here the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word is S
her is the possessive of she
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A reporter focuses on a girl's father, an expert climber.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the centre of NEWSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people renowned as expert climbers and guides on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Career of Conservative replaced by female in March

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter swaps out for the other

parts.note: a procession is a march

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's career ends when a woman takes the seat in March.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month; it is a parade, and swapping its C for F gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A profession is a paid occupation, especially one needing training, which is a career.

clue.text: Discovered pain is back playing rugby

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, stripped of its covering outer letters

parts.note: a twinge is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A painful back was found while playing rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: TWINGE without its outer letters; 'is' is the link. In rugby the backs include the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is one of the back-line positions in a rugby team, playing out wide.

clue.text: "United? Past it" claims Liverpool fan endlessly

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the old word holds the letters

parts.note: aged means old, past it

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: Liverpool FC supporters are called the Reds

explanation.surface: A football fan taunts Manchester United as being over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like Manchester United, the football club, and the Liverpool fan its rival; it means in agreement. Liverpool supporters are the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed means of one mind, unanimous; the question mark admits the stretch from united.

clue.text: Tedious experience meeting Gulf state interpreter

parts.note: a drag is something boring or tiresome
Oman is a state on the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea

explanation.surface: A boring meeting with an interpreter from a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an official interpreter and guide in Arabic, Turkish and Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: Broadcaster's bound to cover opening of remarkable building

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, here with its possessive S

indicators.note: to cover means to lie over and enclose, so the leap surrounds the letter

parts.note: a caper is a playful leap or bound

indicators.note: opening of gives the first letter of the word, an R

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is obliged to report on the launch of an impressive building.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound reads as 'obliged'; it is a leap, CAPER, which takes R inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyscraper is a very tall building of many storeys.

clue.text: This writer's flipping mother produces novel

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me; the 's is 'is'
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An irate writer says his mother has come up with a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's flipping' reads as 'this writer is flipping', not a swear word: the setter, turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a well-meaning matchmaker.

clue.text: Portugal blocks dissent about allowances

indicators.note: blocks means sits in the way, inside the other letters
about means turned around and moved, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Portugal obstructs disagreement over grants.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular payments such as a cleric's salary or student grant.

clue.text: Sign of mostly heavy drinker overindulging

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: hard can mean heavy, as in hard going or a hard blow
a binger is someone drinking to excess in a session

explanation.surface: A warning sign that someone is drinking far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HARD to HAR; the drinker on a binge is a BINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a forerunner or omen, something that signals what is coming.

clue.text: Ross possibly needs time to get tidy

parts.note: Ross Kemp is a British actor, so Ross may stand for his surname

explanation.surface: Someone called Ross needs a while to make themselves presentable.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross Kemp is a British actor, best known from the soap EastEnders; 'possibly' warns that Ross is only one example of a Kemp.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt is the rarely used positive of unkempt: neat, well-groomed.

clue.text: Note cost to house extremely unconvincing asylum seeker

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: to house means to hold something inside, so the fee takes in the letters

parts.note: a fee is a cost or charge

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters of the word, its first and last

parts.note: its outer letters are U and G

explanation.surface: A doubtful claimant for asylum is charged a fee for accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconvincing' looks like it describes the asylum seeker; only its two ends are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is a person who has fled their country and seeks safety and protection elsewhere.

clue.text: Chat with politician protecting city's old street feature

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a guard would, so the chat and politician wrap round the city

parts.note: gas is informal for idle chat
MP, Member of Parliament
LA, Los Angeles, a crossword favourite for city

explanation.surface: A chat with a politician who is guarding a city.
explanation.walkthrough: GAS and MP together surround LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas lamps lit Victorian streets before electric lighting replaced them.

clue.text: First man to tackle teacher leaving area for capital

indicators.note: to tackle here means to grip round, so the first man encloses the letters

parts.note: Adam, the first man in Genesis

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs from the word, which loses it

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: Adam goes in for a tackle on a teacher who is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' suggests football or rugby but means hold round, as a tackler grips an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Around noon, Cornish tourist catches count in London Tube station

indicators.note: around means the other letters go round this one
catches means grabs and holds inside

parts.note: emmet is Cornish dialect for a tourist (literally an ant)
to count on is to bank on, so bank means count

explanation.surface: At midday a holidaymaker in Cornwall catches a count at a London Underground stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Emmet is a word Cornish locals use for tourists. The count is not a nobleman: you count on, or bank on, something.
explanation.definitionFit: Embankment is a London Underground station on the Thames riverside.

clue.text: Mounted rider is enjoying harnesses

indicators.note: harnesses means holds within, so the answer is held across these words

explanation.surface: A horseman on horseback enjoys the horse's tack.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'rideR IS ENjoying'; 'Mounted' looks like a riding word but means gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen and mounted both mean having gone up or climbed higher.

clue.text: Delay entering ground hellish for club, Hibernian

indicators.note: entering means going inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: Postponement at a terrible stadium for the Edinburgh football club Hibernian.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian looks like the Scottish football club; it means Irish. 'for' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shillelagh is a traditional Irish cudgel, often of blackthorn, and Hibernian means Irish.

clue.text: Lifted two items of furniture in sleeping quarters

parts.note: a crib, a baby's cot, is the first of the two pieces
the second piece found in a bedroom is a bed

explanation.surface: Someone raised a pair of furniture pieces in a dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two items of furniture in sleeping quarters' describes both pieces together; 'Lifted' means copied, not raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy dishonestly, as lifting someone else's work or answers is.

clue.text: Falls out of Renault car at a corner heading north

indicators.note: heading north says the hidden letters are read backwards
out of means drawn from inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tumbles out of a Renault at a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Falls out' as the definition, but 'out of' signals the hidden letters, so 'Falls' alone is the definition. Upward in a down clue reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall, such as those on the Nile.

clue.text: Act guards called crazy

indicators.note: guards means encloses to protect, so the act holds the letters

parts.note: a deed is an act
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: An act shields those who rang in, which is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means insane or mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: Wipes last of debts faced by Down family

indicators.note: faced by means the final letter has the other pieces in front of it

parts.note: nap is the soft downy surface of cloth
kin are one's family

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word, an S

explanation.surface: Wiping out the final debts owed by the Down family.
explanation.walkthrough: Down capitalised looks like the Northern Irish county; it is nap, the fluffy surface of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Napkins are cloths or paper squares used to wipe the mouth at meals.

clue.text: Know essentially after tax returns what a carpenter makes?

indicators.note: returns means the combined letters are turned to run backwards
essentially means the heart of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: the middle of the word is NO
net pay is what is left after tax

explanation.surface: A tax return question about what a carpenter produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax returns' looks like a single phrase but is split: 'after tax' is net pay, and 'returns' turns everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue a carpenter cuts to fit a mortise joint; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: What pricy car hire service may do for commercial listings

definitions.text: What pricy car hire service may do
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: rent out Rolls-Royce cars
second meaning: registers of properties and the rents they bring in

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits as a verb and a car brand; the second is the estate agent's term.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent roll is a register of a landlord's properties and tenants with the income each yields.

clue.text: Maybe one more lacking in feeling

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one is an example of a ...
second meaning: comparative of numb, more numb

explanation.walkthrough: The same letters are read as a count and as 'more numb', with a silent B.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an integer, and numb, numbing, number gives the comparative adjective.

clue.text: Broadcast reported rowing crew obtaining drug

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, spoken aloud, so the words are taken by ear

parts.note: reported means said, and an eight is a racing crew of eight rowers: said eight

explanation.surface: A news report of a rowing crew found taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like part of the news story but is the signal that what follows is heard; 'obtaining' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to give them a tranquillising drug.

clue.text: Diet of mine after vacation visiting revolutionary country

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the letters go inside
revolutionary means turning round, so the country reads backwards

parts.note: Niger, the West African country

indicators.note: vacation means emptying, so only the first and last letters of the word remain

parts.note: emptied it leaves ME

explanation.surface: My diet while holidaying in a country that has had a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' could be a parliament, as in Japan, but here it is food; 'vacation' means emptying out, not a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of eating or exercise, which is what a diet is.

clue.text: Warm feeling when farm changes hands

indicators.note: changes hands means right is swapped for left, R becoming L

parts.note: to farm is to grow crops

explanation.surface: A cosy feeling when a farm is sold to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes hands' looks like a sale but swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a feeling of warmth and contentment, as in a glow of pride.

clue.text: Male Cockney brought down spoke indistinctly

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: humbled means brought low

explanation.surface: A man from London's East End was cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so HUMBLED becomes UMBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumble is to speak quietly and unclearly, not opening the mouth properly.

clue.text: Artist using uplifting yellow medium to capture island

indicators.note: to capture means to take inside
uplifting in a down clue means read upwards, so the two pieces run backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic gold or yellow
M is the clothing size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A painter uses a bright yellow paint to depict an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Medium looks like a painting medium; it is M. OR and M read upwards give MRO, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter and sculptor.

clue.text: Top policeman finally pursuing one involved in murder?

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the policeman's letter comes after

parts.note: a group of crows is called a murder, so a crow is one member of it

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word, an N

explanation.surface: A senior police officer chasing a murder suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: A murder is the collective noun for crows; the question mark flags that it is not a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the top of the head, or of a hill or hat.

clue.text: Plant that's big they're developing

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A plant that grows big as they cultivate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is the link; the nine letters of 'big they're' make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wildflower once used in herbal remedies for the eyes.
